clips.title: The story
paras: A shaman travels from the Barrens to the Ruins of Stardust for the final gathering trial in the journey to earn Call of Water. Brine sends the initiate north into Ashenvale to draw pure water from its ancient fountain.

After gathering water from the pool below Brine’s hut in the Barrens and the pure well of Tarren Mill, the shaman needs one final essence. Brine sends the initiate north across the dry plains and into Ashenvale, an ancient woodland sacred to the night elves. The dry Barrens give way to Ashenvale’s deep canopy, where water takes another form. A shaman must understand this variety to live in harmony with the element.

Beyond the shimmering waters of Mystral Lake, near the mountain pass between Ashenvale and the Stonetalon Mountains, lie the Ruins of Stardust. An ancient fountain rests among quiet waters and old stones in this secluded elven sanctum. Untamed elemental and nature spirits guard the ruins and resent intruders. The shaman must tread carefully to draw water from the fountain.

clips.title: Quest text
paras: Take this waterskin and head deep into the lush forest the night elves call Ashenvale. It is to the far north of the Barrens.

Once you've entered the forest, travel west. Along the mountains that separate Stonetalon and Ashenvale, and beyond Lake Mystral, you will find a holy place: the Ruins of Stardust. At the center of the lake you will find a small fountain.
Bring me a sample of the fountain's water. It will be the final component you'll need before I send you back to Islen.

clips.title: Progress
paras: Do you have the water yet, friend? Tales say the ruins were protected by large creatures of nature that do not care for visitors, but those could be myths to scare off the enemies of the night elves.

clips.title: Completion
paras: Wonderful, friend. With all three samples gathered, I can create for you a vial of the purest water any living creature will find. It will be used in the next steps of your rite of passage.
I am pleased to count you among our kind, friend. You do all adventurer proud, and I look forward to hearing about your exploits in the future.
